rows.title: Realtime safety on the audio thread
rows.gaps: rtsan_check (RealtimeSanitizer, ADR-199) runs the real process() over all parameter ids, both engines, morph, intents, mod matrix, MIDI, loads, bypass and reactivation, with a planted fault and a clean control, in verify full; there it is macOS-local and SKIPs without Homebrew LLVM. Neither PR nor push CI (ci.yml) runs it; the nightly does, on GitHub's macOS runner with Homebrew LLVM (job rtsan-legacy-process, ADR-393). The first night green on both runners, run 43205570893 (2026-11-12, commit 8c9521db), ran it green (the macOS leg was green on 11-11 too, run 43007445035): the plant read 1 violation, the clean control 0, and the full seeded schedule 0 (397 parameters, 1,502 process calls). Paths outside its seeded schedule are unproven. For horde 2's engine: h2_rt_lint_check (verify fast) bans nine classes of allocating, locking, blocking or throwing construct under h2/ and engine2/core/ (B535: the clean-room engine, scanned whole with no waiver), with the offline harness exempt and printed and four std::string uses in the frozen swarm core listed as waivers; h2_engine_rtsan_check (verify full, macOS-local like rtsan_check; not in the nightly) runs RealtimeSanitizer over every engine call on the parity scenarios (at least 659, its pinned floor), with a planted allocation. horde 2 has no shell to probe yet: waits on B398, whose acceptance rows are drafted in docs/proposals/h2-shell-acceptance.md.

rows.title: Thread races between UI, host and audio threads
rows.gaps: tsan_stress_check (ADR-200) drives the legacy shell's real entry points from a host-like main thread during render and holds ZERO main-thread write races over 3 seeds; load_handoff_check covers load ordering the sanitizer cannot see. Accepted until the legacy park trigger (ADR-186 section 6): read-only main-thread and host reads of audio-owned state, counted every run. Both run in verify full, macOS-local; tsan_stress_check SKIPs there without Homebrew LLVM (ADR-199). The nightly runs tsan_stress_check on GitHub's macOS runner with Homebrew LLVM (job tsan-stress-handoff, ADR-393; despite its name it runs tsan_stress_check only, not load_handoff_check); on the first night green on both runners, run 43205570893 (2026-11-12, commit 8c9521db), it was green: the write plant and the read plant each read 1 report, the controls 0 on seeds 1 to 3, and the full runs 0 main-thread writes (26, 53 and 57 accepted reads). Since ADR-233 (B505) CI's sanitize (thread) leg runs tsan_stress_check on every PR that touches code or docs/presets/ (ci.yml skips a PR whose every file is a .md, under traces/, or under docs/ outside docs/presets/) with the runner's g++, its must-fire plants first and a SKIP failing the step; load_handoff_check still runs in verify full only. Paths outside the seeded schedule are unproven. horde 2 has no shell yet; ADR-200's shell rules make this harness its gate.

rows.title: NaN, Inf and denormals
rows.gaps: The legacy output guard now latches and counts (nan_latch_check; hostile_events_check reads the real plugin's counter), but the count reaches no user-visible surface yet. horde 2's engine has no output guard: it ends in tanh, and a NaN passes through. Flush-to-zero is ruled ON for the horde 2 shell from its first build (ADR-211; measured, 8 of 543 engine digests change, each sample by less than 4.1e-308), and since 2026-10-12 every gate that replays the engine through the stream replay (tools/h2_engine_stream.h: parity, its FMA control, the self-digests, the engine rtsan probe) runs it with the mode on, set in one shared switch (h2/flush_to_zero.h), with a must-fire line proving it per gate; the eight rows are re-pinned. No shell exists to set it for a host, the switch has never run on Windows, and the switch forces round-to-nearest inside its scope (ADR-213), proved by a must-fire control ROUND line. The engine harness (h2/harness/) does not set the mode yet (h2/README.md), so the gates that render through it, the parameter fuzz and the soak, run with it off. Legacy keeps snapping denormals in software in the swarm and sub cores. The parameter fuzz (h2_fuzz_check, verify full) counts non-finite samples over the engine's ranged keys: none in 12,000 measured cases, and none in the nightly's deep run of 20,000 on Linux x86_64 (run 43205570893 (2026-11-12, commit 8c9521db); through the harness, so with flush-to-zero off), whose two NaN plants were read as planted (888 and 1,709 cases). The horde 2 shell's latch-and-report guard and its user-visible count are ruled (ADR-209 item 7) and wait on B398.
rows.tripwire: NaN events: 0, plus the guard's trip count

rows.title: Sample-rate and block-size dependence
rows.gaps: Rate and block-size checks exist per mechanism. No full matrix rendering each reference patch at 44.1/48/96/192 kHz and blocks of 1, 7, 64, 512 and varying, compared on perceptual features.

rows.title: Long-run drift
rows.gaps: Legacy: stability_check holds RMS drift, f0 drift, peak and non-finite count of the legacy SAW core over 60 simulated seconds in verify full, and over 3,600 per patch in the nightly (job stability-legacy-saw, 9 patches). horde 2's current composed engine (h2/, ADR-187): h2_soak_check holds level drift, DC drift, the clicks and steps at power-of-two frame counts, non-finite samples and silence after release, with nine controls on every run (eight planted faults that must be read, one steady source that must read clean), at its short size in verify full and at two long sizes in the nightly (soak-h2-long, soak-h2-extreme). The first night green on both runners, run 43205570893 (2026-11-12, commit 8c9521db), was green on all three jobs (the 11-11 night, run 43007445035, was cancelled on Linux at its then 120-minute limit): stability 9 of 9 patches; the long cell 14,384 simulated seconds (just under four hours) over 899 windows, the extreme-loud cell 2,384 over 149; every control read as it must (the eight plants found, the steady source clean). Each size's cells rotate by night (every cell of a rotation within three nights); that night ran long-192 and extreme-loud, and the local cell long-min is run by hand only, never in the nightly. Not yet: spectral centroid and pitch are not held on horde 2 (h2_soak_check's header says so); one enrolled engine and one cell per size each night, so not every engine; the clean-room engine is not enrolled; the thresholds are proposed, not ratified (ADR-209 item 5); the reach is bounded: on the long cell a steady level drift is red above 0.336 dB an hour (grey from 0.168) and a DC creep above 0.00452 of the level an hour (grey from 0.00226), on the extreme cell 2.06 dB (grey from 1.03) and 0.0276 (grey from 0.0138), and anything slower than grey is not seen; the legacy run is 3,600 s, not four hours (stability_job.py says why).

rows.title: Numerical stability at the edges
rows.gaps: Legacy: note-stream fuzzing, hostile-event checks and a high-coupling lifecycle probe. horde 2's engine: h2_fuzz_check (verify full; a deep run in the nightly job list) draws seeded cases over the 112 keys the declared table gives a range, with sweeps and stacked changes, and judges every sample for non-finite values, growth, and silence after release; planted faults (blow-up, slow growth, plateau, burst, NaN, hang, misread) must be found on every run. The deep run (nightly job fuzz-h2-engines) first completed with a receipt on run 43205570893 (2026-11-12, commit 8c9521db) (11-11's Linux leg was cancelled at its then 120-minute limit): green, 20,000 cases, 0 problems, 0 grey results, and every planted fault read as planted over the same cases; one enrolled engine, the current composed engine (h2/, ADR-187). Not yet: the clean-room engine is not enrolled, so it is not fuzzed; 24 engine keys have no declared range and are never fuzzed (printed as a hole on every run; 24 on that night); the level bands are a runaway alarm and would pass an engine twice as loud on every patch, so level regression waits on the per-patch measurements (phase 2 package P9); growth that only appears during a sweep is not followed; the thresholds are proposed, not ratified.

rows.title: State and preset compatibility
rows.gaps: Three state fixtures load bit-identically; load_handoff_check holds that a load is whole whether or not the plugin is processing (ADR-200, ADR-208); and param_id_lock_check locks all 397 host-visible parameter ids append-only (removal, renumbering, re-ranging and reuse are red; its full row asks the real plugin). Defaults are deliberately not locked: a default change is caught only by the ADR-and-migration rule in review. No per-release saved-state corpus rendered in CI (nothing is released yet). horde 2 has no parameter manifest, so its lock section is a stub (B308 H4).

rows.title: Host integration edge cases
rows.gaps: pluginval runs at strictness 10 in CI (Windows on every PR, macOS on main pushes). auval is a manual step, not a gate. No clap-validator, scripted host matrix, or two-instance shared-state test.
rows.tripwire: Validators: all green, N hosts tested

rows.title: Perceptual quality not heard on monitors
rows.gaps: A fitted aliasing metric across the keyboard. No per-patch suite for true peak, DC, sub-20 Hz energy or mono-sum loss with stored thresholds.

rows.title: The parity-golden trap
rows.gaps: Parity with the prototypes is provisional under ADR-187. Few closed-form, conservation or metamorphic tests independent of the prototypes, and golden_registry_check now counts them: 1 of 39 goldens carries an independent check, and none is closed-form.
rows.tripwire: Goldens with independent check: N of M

rows.title: Build and platform divergence
rows.gaps: build_flags_check pins the numerics and safety flags of all 108 build targets, and any fast-math-family flag anywhere is red. Pinning found gaps, tracked on B454: the legacy plugin is optimised only when configured as Release, only the native architecture is built on macOS, the build sets no warnings, MSVC gets no floating-point flags from the repo, and the sanitizer loop skips 12 executables. x86_64 is exercised only by CI's Linux verify fast (its host-compiled checks) and sanitizer job, the Windows build and validation, and the nightly's Linux jobs (Release builds of the legacy stability check and the h2 harness with gcc 15.2; green on run 43205570893 (2026-11-12, commit 8c9521db)); no parity run on x86_64 at the shipped Release flags. ADR-209 item 8: the two architectures are macOS arm64 and Windows x64; Intel macOS is not a 1.0 platform.

rows.title: Worst-case CPU and licensing exposure
rows.gaps: license_audit_check holds 11 third-party components (8 ship) against an allow list ratified 2026-10-10 (ADR-205), each license read from the component's own files at its pin. Two exceptions are accepted with expiries (ADR-204, ADR-206); none is pending. The SBOM generator omits three nested shipping components. Ten release questions are open in docs/LICENSES-THIRD-PARTY.md. The B439 budget and the CPU ledger exist as documents, and the CPU measurement is run by hand; no per-release gate on the worst-case patch.
rows.tripwire: Worst-case CPU: X% of budget; Licenses: clear

rows.title: Symptom clamping
rows.gaps: weakening_check counts isfinite, isnan and std::clamp in src/, h2/ and engine2/core/ (B535) and is red on any increase the human has not approved. Since 2026-10-12 that approval must cite a trace with a root-cause section that names the file, and the rule is re-checked on every run; a guard tagged as boundary validation or a latching output guard still needs the approval but no trace (ADR-213). Not yet: min/max nests, ternary and if-assign clamps, tanh-style limits and home-made clamp helpers are unseen until the human approves a one-time re-baseline of 75 lines under h2/; a change that tags an old guard and adds a new untagged one reads the same as an honest new tagged guard, so the approval prints every guard line and the human must read them; a ledger edited by hand skips the approval path
rows.tripwire: New DSP clamps without a root-cause trace: 0

rows.title: Snapshot of the bug
rows.gaps: golden_registry_check (verify fast) discovers every golden and pin by rule and is red for one with no registry entry, for an entry citing a check verify does not run, and for an independence claim with no evidence. Not yet: an entry may still be registered as prototype-parity-only, and 38 of the 39 are, so nothing forces a NEW golden to carry an independent justification; whether bit-identity pins count as goldens is the lead's reading, not yet ruled
rows.tripwire: New goldens without a named justification: 0

rows.title: Tolerance creep
rows.gaps: tolerance_registry_check pins 138 tolerances (ACCEPTANCE.md and the C++ checks) and fails on any unapproved change or unregistered newcomer. Not yet: the JS labs and oracles (.mjs), integer thresholds written inline, tolerances computed from other names; 75 entries have no governing ADR yet; it cannot prove an `approved` reference came from the human.

rows.title: Quiet disabling
rows.gaps: test_table_check makes every check declare whether ./verify runs it, and cross-checks the claim. weakening_check counts skips, suppressions, disabled sanitizers, soft-fails, UNWIRED declarations and DSP guards against a baseline and fails on any increase. Every golden-parity gate now fails below a pinned scenario count, so a corpus cannot shrink quietly (parity_floor_check and in-source floors, thirteen gates; found by the 2026-10-10 audit). Not yet: markers assembled by macro, and proof that an `approved` reference was written by the human rather than an agent.
rows.tripwire: Skips, suppressions and disabled sanitizers: no increase
